message: foundry_verify scans the whole repo for every constraint on every task, and a constraint cannot declare "active from task X". On a brownfield repo whose pre-existing code already violates seeded constraints, the planner has to relocate legacy code outside the scanned paths, and has to defer regression-lock constraints to gate tasks that edit docs/foundry.json mid-flight. A per-constraint "since"/"activeFrom" task ID, or a baseline of pre-existing hits, would remove that workaround.

P0-16 asks to push the branch and check CI via gh. git push fails with "ERROR: This repository was archived so it is read-only" (same failure foundry_run_start reported as basePush at flight start). gh is installed and authenticated, but there is nothing to check CI against since the push never lands. This is an operator-level GitHub repo state issue, not something fixable from the worktree; logging it here so it's visible without blocking the task.

foundry_verify runs composer test (which does a fresh wp-env DB install) against the same shared test database as any other composer test invocation I have running. When I ran one in the background and called foundry_verify concurrently, both processes hit the same MySQL tables mid-install, producing spurious "table doesn't exist" and deadlock failures across unrelated tests (P1-08). No code defect; re-running foundry_verify alone was clean. Cost ~10 minutes diagnosing before realizing it was a self-inflicted concurrency issue, not a regression.
